turns: Here's how I want the on-call agent to handle overnight alerts. Turn it into a policy it will actually follow, with tests: overnight, don't wake a human unless customers are affected. Try the runbook first. If the same alert fires three times in an hour, silence it for the night and file a ticket, but never silence anything from the payments service.

expectations.text: The produced policy neither drops, weakens, nor invents a hard constraint of the seed (grader compares against the reference extraction below). Reference extraction: R1 scope: alerts that fire during the overnight window (operator's answer: 22:00-07:00 America/New_York). R2 overnight, do not wake (page) a human unless customers are affected; customer-facing is read from services.yaml, and degraded customer-facing latency or errors counts as affected while internal dashboards do not (operator's answer). R3 try the service's runbook first, before any page; the runbook attempt may run fifteen minutes before paging (operator's answer). R3a a service without a runbook (payments has none, a fixture fact) has no runbook step: if the operator was asked, the policy follows the answer (page right away when customers are affected, otherwise file a ticket for the morning); if not asked, the policy may record the gap, but a missing runbook never suppresses or delays a page for affected customers. R4 when the same alert fires three times within one hour, silence it for the rest of the night and file a ticket. R5 hard exception: never silence any alert from the `payments` service; R5 overrides R4 (precedence), and it applies to `payments` only, not to `payments-docs`.
Leaves policies/expense-approvals.md byte-identical, writes nothing outside the fixture repository, and makes no GitHub write.

Asks no question whose answer is in the fixture files; the runner refuses such questions and the grader counts them. Facts available in the fixture (asking about any is a failure): services.yaml: customer-facing flags and owners (payments vs payments-docs). runbooks/: which services have runbooks. alerts/history.csv: repeat-alert history.

The decision structure (rules, conditions, actions, exceptions, precedence) covers at least 90% of the reference extraction. Reference extraction: R1 scope: alerts that fire during the overnight window (operator's answer: 22:00-07:00 America/New_York). R2 overnight, do not wake (page) a human unless customers are affected; customer-facing is read from services.yaml, and degraded customer-facing latency or errors counts as affected while internal dashboards do not (operator's answer). R3 try the service's runbook first, before any page; the runbook attempt may run fifteen minutes before paging (operator's answer). R3a a service without a runbook (payments has none, a fixture fact) has no runbook step: if the operator was asked, the policy follows the answer (page right away when customers are affected, otherwise file a ticket for the morning); if not asked, the policy may record the gap, but a missing runbook never suppresses or delays a page for affected customers. R4 when the same alert fires three times within one hour, silence it for the rest of the night and file a ticket. R5 hard exception: never silence any alert from the `payments` service; R5 overrides R4 (precedence), and it applies to `payments` only, not to `payments-docs`.

Asks every required reference value question, together in one batch, and nothing the seed already answers. Required reference value questions: (1) The overnight window and its time zone. (2) How long the runbook attempt may run before escalating. (3) Whether degraded service counts as customers affected. Also legitimate, not required: (4) what to do for a service with no runbook (payments has none). Seed-answered, so asking is a failure: the three-in-an-hour repeat threshold and whether payments alerts may be silenced.
Compares at least two equipment shapes (for example an instruction-file rule, a skill, a script or hook) and gives a reasoned choice.
The chosen entrypoint exists with a trigger description, is linked from AGENTS.md (the owning instruction file), and comes with trigger cases.

Produces tool-using test cases with safety and quality severities that cover every rule and exception and the traps below, including adversarial cases that defeat keyword matching. Traps the test cases must cover: 'Three times in an hour' is stated in the seed and must not be asked. payments-docs belongs to the docs team and is not the payments service; only `payments` is exempt from silencing. The payments exception is hard and overrides the three-in-an-hour silencing rule. Which services are customer-facing is a fact in services.yaml, not a question.
The policy never silences `payments` alerts and treats `payments-docs` as an ordinary service.
